hero.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle
hero.date: Available since Thu Apr 9, 2026 — NOW STREAMING
hero.about: First film in the three-part Infinity Castle trilogy that picks up the Demon Slayer storyline post–Hashira Training Arc. Tanjiro, Nezuko, the Hashira, and the entire Demon Slayer Corps are dragged into Muzan Kibutsuji's mirrored stronghold for the long-awaited final showdown. Adapts the manga's climactic arc. The theatrical run shattered Japanese box-office records (¥40B+) before quietly arriving on Crunchyroll in April. Subbed and English-dubbed.
hero.why: Tier 2 hero — Loved-list AND watchlist title that's been streamable for ~5 weeks but slipped past prior recs. This is the highest-priority unwatched pick on the board right now: Demon Slayer is on your Loved list, you pinned Infinity Castle specifically, and it's a 2.5-hour film that fits a weekend bedtime block. Recommend pairing it with Saturday rather than splitting across two nights.

new_this_week.title: Black Phone 2
new_this_week.about: Scott Derrickson returns to direct this sequel to 2021's The Black Phone. Finney (Mason Thames) and Gwen (Madeleine McGraw) face The Grabber (Ethan Hawke) again — this time through dreams. Adapts a Joe Hill short story. R-rated.
new_this_week.why: Horror/Suspense is in your top-4 genre stack. 80% RT critic / 82% audience on theatrical run, $132M worldwide. Drops Saturday — fits the bedtime horror slot if you want a Sat-night alt to the Demon Slayer block.

new_this_week.title: The Boroughs
new_this_week.about: Eight-episode sci-fi horror series executive-produced by the Duffer Brothers. In a picturesque retirement community, unlikely heroes — played by Geena Davis, Alfred Molina, Alfre Woodard, Bill Pullman, Clarke Peters, Denis O'Hare — band together against an otherworldly threat that's stealing their time.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi + supernatural + ensemble + Stranger Things pedigree is a direct match on multiple signals. Easily the most anticipated new series of the week.

new_this_week.about: Episode 5 of the 10-episode small-town supernatural mystery. Ep 6 follows the next week; May 27 is a two-ep drop.

new_this_week.title: Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed
new_this_week.about: Tatiana Maslany leads a darkly comedic thriller as a newly divorced mom convinced she witnessed a crime while spiraling through custody battles, identity crisis, and youth-soccer politics. 30-min eps, weekly through July 15.
new_this_week.why: Dark comedy + 30-min + strong ensemble lead lines up with your Fleabag/Slow Horses shelf. Try-flag because early critic reviews are still embargoed.

new_this_week.title: Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan: Ghost War
new_this_week.about: Standalone Jack Ryan film with John Krasinski returning to the title role. Continues the spy-thriller world from the Prime series.
new_this_week.why: Spy thriller is Slow Horses-adjacent. Try-flag because Jack Ryan TV had uneven plotting; the film format may help tighten the pacing.

new_this_week.title: Spider-Noir
new_this_week.about: Live-action Marvel Spider-Man Noir. Nic Cage as Ben Reilly, an older down-on-his-luck PI in 1930s New York forced back into the cowl. Released in 'Authentic Black and White' and 'True-Hue Full Color' versions.
new_this_week.why: RT flagged it as #1 most-anticipated TV of May. Period noir + Cage is a distinctive swing — high-variance try.

new_this_week.title: Kevin
new_this_week.about: Adult animation about a cat dropped into an Astoria pet rescue after his owners break up. Schwartzman voices Kevin; Plaza, Whoopi Goldberg, John Waters in supporting roles.
new_this_week.why: Watchlist title that's still sitting — Schwartzman + Plaza + John Waters is exactly your off-beat shelf. Bedtime-friendly 30-min eps.

new_this_week.title: Lord of the Flies
new_this_week.about: Jack Thorne's 4-part adaptation of Golding's novel. Boys, plane crash, descent. Critics 92–94%, audience 54% — audience complaints flag intrusive score and stylized camerawork.
new_this_week.why: Try, not strong. Book adaptation + 4-ep run hits your signals, but the audience divide ('artsy', 'heavy-handed') is exactly your misses-signals flag. Worth a single-night Ep 1 sample.

new_this_week.title: Star City
new_this_week.about: Spinoff from 'For All Mankind' from Ben Nedivi, Matt Wolpert, Ronald D. Moore. Alt-history space race told from the Soviet side — cosmonauts, engineers, intelligence officers in Star City. Two-ep premiere, weekly through Jul 10.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi (your #1 genre) + alt-history + world-building stack — Foundation/Severance-adjacent prestige sci-fi shelf. Mark for May 29 dive.

new_this_week.title: Citadel S2
new_this_week.about: Husband-wife spy duo regain wiped memories and resume the fight against rival agency Manticore. S2 of the Russo-produced franchise.
new_this_week.why: Spy thriller, Slow Horses-adjacent shelf, big-budget set pieces. Try-flag because S1 was a mixed-reception swing.

new_this_week.title: Unconditional
new_this_week.about: Israeli thriller: a 23-year-old is arrested for drug smuggling in Moscow; her mother refuses to accept the charges and is pulled into a deadly web of crime and corruption. Subtitled.
new_this_week.why: International thrillers are a strong wildcard for you. Worth a single-episode test.

new_this_week.title: Jujutsu Kaisen S3
new_this_week.about: Post-Shibuya Incident — Yuji, Megumi, and Yuta navigate the brutal Culling Game. Crunchyroll's #1 most-anticipated of Spring 2026.
new_this_week.why: Demon Slayer-adjacent — supernatural + action + sub-30-min eps. Try-flag because shonen volume can run long.

new_this_week.title: Re:ZERO S3
new_this_week.about: Fantasy isekai with a time-loop hook — Subaru relives deaths to alter outcomes. S3 returns after a long gap.
new_this_week.why: Fantasy + plot-puzzle mechanics — fits your fantasy/sci-fi top stack and 'plot twists that pay off' signal. Try-flag: S1 is required watching.
